claims: "Integrity" is the official name of the Orion spacecraft capsule used for the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis II mission carries four astronauts on a 10-day round trip around the Moon.
The Artemis II crew chose the name "Integrity".
"Integrity" serves as the Artemis II crew's callsign.
The Integrity spacecraft is the first crewed spacecraft to fly around the Moon since 1972.
The Integrity capsule safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen were the four crew members aboard the Integrity capsule.
The Artemis II astronauts suggested naming a lunar crater "Integrity" to mark their mission.
